definitions.title: Cross (Vector) Product
definitions.latex: \mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ u_1 & u_2 & u_3 \\ v_1 & v_2 & v_3 \end{vmatrix} = (u_2 v_3 - u_3 v_2)\mathbf{i} - (u_1 v_3 - u_3 v_1)\mathbf{j} + (u_1 v_2 - u_2 v_1)\mathbf{k}
definitions.statement: The cross product of two 3D vectors u and v is a vector orthogonal to both u and v, with direction given by the right-hand rule, and magnitude equal to the area of the parallelogram determined by u and v.
conditions: Anti-commutative: u x v = -(v x u)
definitions.explanation: Unlike the dot product which returns a scalar, the cross product constructs a mutually perpendicular vector in 3-space.
definitions.keyTakeaway: |u x v| = |u| |v| sin(theta); u x v = 0 if and only if u and v are parallel.

definitions.title: Scalar Triple Product and Parallelepiped Volume
definitions.latex: (\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}) \cdot \mathbf{w} = \begin{vmatrix} u_1 & u_2 & u_3 \\ v_1 & v_2 & v_3 \\ w_1 & w_2 & w_3 \end{vmatrix}, \quad V = |(\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v}) \cdot \mathbf{w}|
definitions.statement: The absolute value of the scalar triple product computes the volume of the parallelepiped determined by u, v, and w. Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product is zero.
definitions.explanation: Combines cross and dot products into a single 3x3 determinant measuring 3D volume.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Zero scalar triple product indicates linear dependency (coplanarity) of three vectors.
